analysis: What changed vs the 5 AM brief: futures firmed further into the holiday — S&P +0.72% and Nasdaq +1.11% as of 06:06 ET vs +0.4%/+0.5% an hour earlier — and Wednesday's breadth detail filled in: roughly 370 advancers vs 128 decliners with 8 of 11 sectors higher, so the comeback was broad, not just index-level. The genuinely new items since 5 AM are the tariff clarification (new levies replace rather than add to existing ones — a real de-escalation of the double-tariff fear), the Bank of England's warning that AI financing scale threatens financial stability, Deutsche Bank's S&P 9,000-by-end-2027 call, the BOJ's Tamura pushing timely hikes, and the HPQ earnings detail (revenue $16.0B vs ~$15.4B expected, EPS $0.83 vs $0.75, dividend raised, Emma Walmsley named CEO from Jan 2027). Nvidia's Wednesday round trip — a 9.1% slide turning into a 1.3% gain — is the single best illustration of the session. Signal vs noise: the tariff clarification, the broad breadth, and the HPQ beat are signal; the BOE warning and Deutsche Bank's 9,000 target are framing, not a trade; any single futures tick on a closed holiday morning is noise, and Friday's thin half session can amplify the first move either way. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads added signal beyond the headlines this morning, so community_signals is empty.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: US index futures strengthen further on Thanksgiving morning: S&P 500 futures +0.72% to 7,247.75, Nasdaq futures +1.11% to 26,389.75, Dow futures +0.37% to 50,415 as of 06:06 ET, extending Wednesday's late rebound.
headlines.why_it_matters: Futures are firmer than an hour ago — the dip-buying momentum is holding into the holiday pause, though overnight futures do not guarantee Friday's open.

headlines.headline: New US tariffs on China and dozens of other nations will replace rather than add to previous ones, clarifying the tariff proposal that rattled markets Wednesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: Removes the double-tariff fear — the worst-case read on the proposal is off the table, a sentiment tailwind into Friday's reopen.

headlines.headline: Bank of England warns the scale and breadth of AI financing poses a threat to financial stability.
headlines.why_it_matters: A central bank putting AI-linked leverage on the stability watchlist keeps the valuation-and-debt debate alive — the same debate behind Wednesday's selloff.

headlines.headline: Deutsche Bank sees the tech rout easing and the S&P 500 reaching 9,000 by end-2027 as focus shifts from AI capital expenditure to monetization.
headlines.why_it_matters: A major bank's long-horizon bull case gives the rebound narrative a second leg — but it is a 13-month view, not a read on Friday's tape.

headlines.headline: BOJ's Tamura urges timely rate hikes, bolstering the case for a Bank of Japan move in December.
headlines.why_it_matters: Another central bank leaning hawkish alongside the Fed's near-certain December hike — global tightening pressure stays in the backdrop.

headlines.headline: HP Inc (HPQ) jumped 11.5% Wednesday after beating Q4 FY26: revenue $16.0B (+9.3% y/y) vs ~$15.4B expected, EPS $0.83 vs $0.75 expected, quarterly dividend raised to $0.31, FY27 guidance $3.15-$3.45, and Emma Walmsley named next CEO from Jan 2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: Company execution overrode a weak tape — HPQ was Wednesday's standout gainer while chips sold off; a reminder that earnings still move single names even in a macro-driven rout.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) swung from a 9.1% intraday slide to a 1.3% gain on Wednesday, the sharpest illustration of the session's reversal; Anthropic rallied 12% off its session lows.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI bellwether's round trip shows dip-buying arrived in the names that sold off hardest — the key tell for whether Wednesday's low holds into Friday.

headlines.headline: Gold pushes higher to $3,602.90 and Bitcoin holds $60,819 as havens and crypto stabilize alongside equities; Brent crude holds near Wednesday's highs around $94.30.
headlines.why_it_matters: Metals and crypto stabilizing alongside equities suggests the risk-off pressure is easing across assets, not just in stocks.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. Carry-forward: Zacks raised its FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24), FY2027 at $1.31; a Seeking Alpha analysis calls USAC a buy at $23.63, citing the 8.9% yield backed by 1.67x distribution coverage and record pricing. Units traded ~$23.14 Wednesday, near the 52-week low of $22.65. Q3 2026 (Nov 3): revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6; $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
